questions.title: Defining the product of an enzymatic reaction
questions.question: In an enzymatic reaction how is the product defined?

options.A: The biomolecule acted upon by an enzyme
options.B: Result of reaction between enzyme and substrate
options.C: The initial unstable transition state molecule
options.D: The specific cofactor organically attached to the enzyme molecule

explanations.A: Incorrect. The molecule an enzyme acts upon at the start is the SUBSTRATE, not the product — this describes the beginning of the reaction, not its result.
explanations.B: Correct. An enzymatic reaction has three basic terms. The substrate is what the enzyme acts on at the start, the transition state is a brief high-energy intermediate mid-reaction, and the product is what the substrate becomes once the enzyme has finished acting on it — the result of the reaction between enzyme and substrate.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The transition state is a fleeting, high-energy intermediate the substrate passes through mid-reaction, not the final, stable result the reaction produces.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A cofactor, when one is needed, is a separate helper molecule the enzyme uses during catalysis, not the product of the reaction itself.

questions.learning_objective: Define the product of an enzymatic reaction as the result of enzyme acting on substrate.
